Part I — Knowledge Base (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 101, English)
The Kul Devata Tarang Check, the Power of the Deepak, and a Warning Against Fake Godmen

This session is a live "tarang" (wavelength/connection) check — a r oll call comparing each devotee's per centage of connection to their kul devata (family deity) against their prior r eading — interwoven with teaching on the power of consistent lamp (deepak) practice, how these per centage r eadings actually work, and a firm warning against tr eating any teacher (including the speaker) as a dir ect mouthpiece for Hanuman ji Maharaj.
Part A — Opening

1. Session framing: The speaker opens by telling the group today's session will focus specifically on checking "tarang" (wavelength/connection strength to one's kul devata) for as many devotees as time allows, promising to move quickly .

2. A moment of encouragement: A devotee (V ani behen) is spontaneously credited by others in the group as a source of inspiration, prompting a round of "Jai Siyaram" and "Jai Gurudev" chanting before the roll call begins.
Part B — The Tarang Roll Call (Summarized)

1. Format: Devotees are called one by one; the speaker states their previous recorded percentage of kul devata tarang connection alongside today's updated reading, along with brief remarks on their practice (deepak/lamp lighting, jaap, havan completion).

2. Overall pattern observed: Across the roll call (roughly twenty devotees checked in this session), those who reported consistent daily deepak lighting, ongoing jaap, and completed havan generally showed meaningful increases — some nearly doubling their percentage (for example, moving from the high-teens/twenties into the high-twenties/thirties, or from the fifties into the sixties/seventies) — while a few devotees whose practice had lapsed, or who had not yet completed their havan, showed little or no change between readings.

3. Devotees nearing or reaching "siddhi": A handful of devotees with long-standing, consistent deepak and havan practice were reported in the 65–75% range, described as having achieved or nearly achieved "kul devata siddhi" (attainment/manifestation of the family deity's grace) in their home.

4. The speaker's r esponse to differing levels of effort: Devotees whose percentages were low and flat were reassured this reflects an absence of visible incentive to push harder rather than any personal failing ("aapki koi galti nahi hai"), while those already seeing results were encouraged that visible progress is precisely what motivates greater ef fort — described as a natural, expected cycle rather than unfairness.
Part C — The Power of the Deepak (Lamp)

1. Deepak as a pur e, non-transactional offering: The speaker teaches that lighting a lamp gives nothing away in the way food, money , or a physical of fering does — it is described as an unusually powerful, purely devotional source of connection precisely because of this.

2. The 108-day pr omise: Per this teaching, consistently lighting 108 lamps (framed as roughly 108 days of daily lighting) with sincere sankalp, without any other elaborate practice, is said to be enough to bring siddhi (spiritual attainment/manifestation) into a devotee's home.

3. Alternatives if lighting a lamp at home isn't possible: Devotees who cannot maintain a lamp at home (for practical or household reasons) are told they may have one lit on their behalf at Ashaeiynn, where a continuous ("akhand") flame is maintained.

4. An illustrative case: The speaker cites a devotee based in Canada whose consistent daily deepak practice alone (without extensive additional ritual) is credited with clearing four generations of pitru dosh within 108 days, alongside gaining dristi and darshan experiences.

5. What "akhand deepak" means: "Akhand" means "unbroken" — an akhand deepak is one kept burning continuously without interruption. Per this teaching, a lamp needs to burn at least 10–12 continuous hours to register as "akhand" for measurement purposes.

6. Short-duration lamps still matter , but measur e differently: An 1 1-day lamp lit for a fixed short duration each day does not register on the tarang measurement scale used for kul devata connection, but is still described as ef fective for negativity/pitruclearing purposes, which is tracked separately .

7. Why kul devata offerings take time to r egister: Per this teaching, an of fering (bhog) made toward one's kul devata takes roughly two months and 22 days to travel and register , since kul devata exist outside Ashaeiynn's direct jurisdiction, in their own separate realm; devotees are advised to wait out this full period before requesting a fresh tarang check.
Part D — What the Per centage Readings Actually Measur e

1. Not a literal divine hotline: The speaker is explicit that these percentage readings do not come from directly measuring the deity , nor from any direct conversation with the kul devata or with Hanuman ji Maharaj. What is measured is a devotee's relative displacement (movement) from their own prior reference point, using a "scale" described as given by Baba and interpreted with the help of saints.

2. A "befor e and after ," not an absolute grade: The percentage shared reflects how far a devotee has shifted from where they previously stood, not an absolute or complete measure of divine grace itself.

3. Explicit denial of speaking dir ectly with Hanuman ji Maharaj: The speaker states plainly that he does not converse directly with Hanuman ji Maharaj, explaining that direct contact of that kind would be instantly overwhelming ("jinda bhasm ho jaayenge" — instantly consumed). What is received instead is described as indications or "thrown fragments" of guidance, perceived through the grace of the guru parampara and saints.

4. A warning about fake godmen: Referencing the rise of imitators following the popularity of certain other spiritual figures, the speaker firmly rejects any claim — by himself or by anyone else — that Hanuman ji Maharaj is literally "in someone's pocket" giving direct verbal instructions, framing such claims as a form of showmanship that damages the reputation of genuine saints and lineages.

5. What closeness to Hanuman ji Maharaj actually r equires: Per this teaching, referencing the Hanuman Chalisa line "Sumire Pawan Sut Pawan Nama," true closeness to Hanuman ji Maharaj belongs only to someone whose mouth carries Ram's name day and night through sustained sadhna — not to anyone claiming shortcut access.

6. Reaffirmed lineage and mantra details: As taught previously , the community identifies as Nath sampradaya Ram bhakts; the mantra "Jai Siyaram" has Sita Mata as rishi, is set in Gayatri chhand, with "Ram" as beej, "Rim" as shakti, and "Ram" as keelak. Hanuman ji Maharaj's presence at the community's guru-sthan (guru position) is described as a standing vow ("vachan"), not evidence of literal ongoing dictation.

7. On dramatics and showmanship: The speaker criticizes public displays of devotion performed for attention ("drama-baazi"), arguing this damages the reputation of genuine gurus and lineages, and encourages devotees to practice quietly in a corner rather than publicize their sadhna.

8. Gurudev's standing vow: The speaker reiterates that his own Gurudev has vowed to continue teaching from this site for seven generations, attributing this to Hanuman ji Maharaj's continued presence there in an awakened (jagrit), guru form.
Part E — Closing Q&A

1. On requesting a mentor's personal contact publicly: A devotee asked how to reach another devotee (V ani behen) privately; the group was reminded not to request personal timing/contact details in a lar ge public session, since doing so invites everyone present to call at once — better handled by searching the group's shared contact list.

2. Highest kul devata tarang per centage ever recorded: Per this teaching, roughly 80% is the highest ever observed; siddhi is generally recognized starting around the 70% mark; 100% has never been seen and may not be attainable.

3. Sankalp and a continuous 24-hour lamp: A devotee asked whether daily sankalp is needed if an akhand (24-hour continuous) lamp is already kept lit for the kul devata alongside ongoing jaap. Per this teaching, sankalp should be taken once at the time the continuous lamp is first lit; if the lamp goes out and must be relit, sankalp should be retaken at that point — a fresh sankalp is not required daily as long as the lamp remains continuously lit.

4. What does "kul devata siddhi" actually mean? This specific question was deflected in-session, with devotees directed to the existing Mool Tatva video library for the full explanation rather than having it repeated live.

5. Closing note on r epeated questions: The speaker notes that some topics have already been explained at length in prior Mool Tatva sessions and encourages devotees to search the app for these existing explanations rather than expecting them repeated live every time, while reaf firming continued openness to follow-up conversation.
6. Session close: The session closes with "Jai Siyaram" chanting and a farewell ("chalte chalte milte rahenge" — we'll keep meeting as we go).
QUICK RULES SUMMARY

Consistent deepak (lamp) practice, jaap, and completed havan are the practices most associated with rising kul devata tarang percentages; lapsed practice or incomplete havan tends to show flat readings. Lighting a lamp is framed as an especially pure, non-transactional devotional of fering; 108 days of consistent lamp-lighting with sincere sankalp is said to be enough on its own to bring siddhi into a home. Devotees unable to maintain a lamp at home may have one lit on their behalf at Ashaeiynn's continuous (akhand) flame. "Akhand" (unbroken) requires at least 10–12 continuous hours of burning to register on the tarang measurement scale; shorter fixed-duration lamps (e.g., 1 1-day cycles) still help with negativity/pitru clearing, tracked separately . Kul devata of ferings take roughly two months and 22 days to register , since kul devata exist outside Ashaeiynn's direct jurisdiction — wait out this period before requesting a fresh check.

Percentage readings measure a devotee's relative displacement from their own prior state, not a literal, absolute divine measurement — mentors do not converse directly with the kul devata or Hanuman ji Maharaj. No teacher , including the speaker , claims direct verbal access to Hanuman ji Maharaj "on demand" — be skeptical of anyone (including imitator "godmen") claiming this. Practice quietly rather than performing devotion publicly for attention; showmanship damages the reputation of genuine gurus and lineages. Sankalp for a continuous 24-hour lamp is taken once at lighting, and again only if the lamp goes out and must be relit — not required as a separate daily ritual. Historically , the highest recorded kul devata tarang percentage is around 80%; siddhi is generally recognized starting around 70%.

Bot Response Guidelines

Present the tarang percentage system, the deepak/108-day teaching, and the of fering-timing framework (roughly two months and 22 days) as this teaching's own devotional framework, not as independently verifiable claims. Always preserve the explicit distinction this session draws between "receiving guidance/indications through grace" and "directly conversing with a deity" — never phrase bot answers in a way that implies the speaker or anyone else claims literal, on-demand divine dictation. If a user asks what "kul devata siddhi" means in full detail, note that this was deflected live in favor of the existing Mool Tatva video library , and avoid inventing a fuller explanation not present in the source material. The roll call of individual devotee percentages is summarized in aggregate in Part I rather than reproduced name-by-name; do not present it as an exhaustive per -person record. Spelling note: the institute's name is written "Ashaeiynn" — use this spelling consistently .
Part III — Curated Conversational Q&A (Hinglish)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Curated Conversational Q&A (Session 101, Hinglish)
The Kul Devata Tarang Check, the Power of the Deepak, and a Warning Against Fake Godmen

This is NOT an exhaustive transcript of every exchange in this session. Only conversations judged genuinely valuable and likely to benefit futur e users ar e included, each with a short italicized note explaining why it was kept. This session is mostly a live roll-call check-in, so Part III her e focuses on the closing Q&A segment wher e reusable, generally-applicable questions came up.
Exchange 1 — Requesting a Mentor's Contact Privately

Devotee: Bhaiya, Vani behen se contact kaise karein? Bhaiya: Aise public session mein kisi ka personal timing ya contact mat maanga karo, warna sab log ek saath call karne lagenge. Group ki shared contact list mein search kar lo.

Why this is her e: A small but genuinely useful piece of community etiquette — a practical answer any devotee might need when trying to privately r each a mentor without disrupting a lar ge gr oup session.
Exchange 2 — Sankalp for a Continuous Lamp

Devotee: Agar main apne kul devata ke liye akhand (24-hour) deepak jalati rahoon, aur jaap bhi chal raha ho, toh kya roz sankalp lena zaroori hai? Bhaiya: Nahi — sankalp ek baar lena hai, jab pehli baar deepak jalao. Agar deepak bujh jaaye aur dobara jalana pade, tabhi dobara sankalp lena. Jab tak deepak lagatar jal raha hai, roz alag se sankalp lene ki zaroorat nahi hai.
Why this is her e: A pr ecise, easily-misunderstood practical rule about akhand deepak practice that devotees ar e likely to ask about repeatedly — worth having documented clearly .
Exchange 3 — The Highest Per centage Ever Recorded

Devotee: Sabse zyada kul devata tarang percentage kitna record hua hai ab tak? Bhaiya: Lagbhag 80% — sabse zyada abhi tak. Siddhi generally 70% ke aas-paas se maani jaati hai. 100% kabhi dekha nahi gaya, aur shayad possible bhi nahi hai.
Why this is her e: Gives devotees a concr ete, honest sense of r ealistic expectations and scale for this practice, dir ectly from the teacher , rather than an assumed or exaggerated benchmark.
Note on Curation

This session was almost entirely a live individual roll call of kul devata tarang percentages, which is summarized in aggregate in Part I rather than reproduced name-by-name, since it consists of personal practice data for roughly twenty devotees rather than conversational teaching content. Only the closing Q&A segment produced exchanges of durable, general value, and those are the three included above.
